name: org.openinjury/openinjury
title: OpenInjury
description: OSHA injury reports from named US worksites and employers, with computed and BLS rates.

tools.name: search_worksites
tools.description: Find worksites by name, with optional state, city or NAICS industry code. Results are ordered by name match, then by name, never by rate. Returns name, address, industry, site_id and the latest year reported.

query.description: Worksite or company name, at least two characters.

limit.description: How many results to return, 25 at most.

tools.name: get_worksite
tools.description: The injury summary a worksite filed with OSHA for each year, the computed rates, the range, the BLS national rate and the comparison, with caveats and sources.

tools.name: get_employer
tools.description: Totals across the worksites that filed under one employer tax ID, by year, how many worksites the totals are based on, and the first 50 worksites by name.

employer_id.description: The employer_id from a worksite record.

ein.description: The employer tax ID, nine digits.

tools.name: get_parent_company
tools.description: Returns a parent company and the employers linked to it, with the public record that proves each link. The record is either a GLEIF relationship record, where parent_id is an LEI, or the parent's SEC Exhibit 21 subsidiary list, where parent_id is a 10-digit SEC CIK. By name, it returns up to 25 parent companies of either kind whose name starts with the given text. A GLEIF parent also includes the Wikidata item that states its LEI as a crosswalk.

parent_id.description: Use the parent company's LEI (20 characters) from a /company page.

name.description: Use the start of a parent company's name (3 characters or more).

tools.name: compare_worksites
tools.description: The tool puts two to four worksites side by side. It shows the latest figures filed with OSHA, the three-year rate with its range, and the BLS national rate. It lists worksites in the order given, never by rate. When two ranges overlap, the answer says the figures do not show a difference.

tools.name: get_industry_benchmark
tools.description: The BLS national injury rate for a NAICS industry code, by year and by establishment size class, with quartiles where BLS publishes them.

year.description: Reference year, 2016 to 2025. The latest year when omitted.

tools.name: list_industries
tools.description: The tool lists NAICS industry codes with an industry page, the industry name, and the number of worksites with a page. You can filter by a word in the name or by the start of the code. The tool returns at most 50 rows in code order.

query.description: Worksite or company name, at least two characters.

limit.description: How many results to return, 25 at most.

tools.name: find_contractors
tools.description: The tool lists worksites in one state and one NAICS trade code in name order, never by rate. It shows each worksite's three-year rate, range, and hours. You can use the list to build a shortlist for vetting, then read each worksite's own record.

min_hours.description: Leave out worksites with fewer total hours over the three years.

limit.description: How many results to return, 25 at most.

offset.description: How many results to skip for the next page.

tools.name: get_inspections
tools.description: OSHA lists inspections opened since 2012 for one worksite or by year across one employer's worksites. For one worksite, the tool returns the latest 25 inspections with totals. It returns inspection type, citation items by class (serious, willful, repeat, other), initial and current penalties, and whether citations are contested or final. It includes only inspections whose name and street address match the worksite. A contested or non-final citation is OSHA's allegation, not a finding.

employer_id.description: The employer_id from a worksite record.

tools.name: get_severe_injuries
tools.description: OSHA severe injury reports cover in-patient hospitalization, amputation, and loss of an eye. The tool counts reports by year for one worksite or sums them across one employer's worksites. It covers Federal OSHA states only, from 2015 to November 2025. It counts only reports whose name and street address match the worksite. It returns no report text or detail about the injured worker.

employer_id.description: The employer_id from a worksite record.

tools.name: search_mines
tools.description: Search MSHA's open government data by mine name, operator name or controller name, or by exact MSHA mine ID, optionally in one state. The tool returns each mine's ID, name, operator, controller, county, state, mine type, commodity and MSHA status. It holds only mines with operator hours reported to MSHA for 2016 or a later year. It orders results by name, then mine ID, never by rate or by count.

query.description: Mine, operator or controller name (at least two characters), or an MSHA mine ID.

limit.description: How many results to return, 25 at most.

tools.name: get_mine
tools.description: Get one mine's record from MSHA open government data by year since 2016. The record includes operator employee hours, operator and contractor employee injuries as reported to MSHA with degree codes 01 to 06, the injury rate per 200,000 hours for a full year with 20,000 hours or more, inspections and inspection hours, violations with significant and substantial and contested counts, with vacated ones left out, proposed, current and paid penalties, controller and operator history with dates, and the source file of every figure.

mine_id.description: MSHA mine ID, up to seven digits.

tools.name: get_mine_controller
tools.description: Get one mine controller's record from MSHA open government data. The record sums hours, injuries as reported to MSHA, violations and penalties by year across the mines it held for the most days of each year. It lists the mines it has controlled, showing the first 50 by name and the dates it held each. The tool returns only companies; MSHA controllers that are individual persons have no record here.

controller_id.description: MSHA controller ID, as shown on a mine record.

tools.name: get_coverage
tools.description: The tool shows who must report to OSHA, how many worksites filed, and how that compares with all establishments in the Census County Business Patterns count, nationally or for one state. With a NAICS code, it also shows the number of worksites with a page in that industry.

tools.name: get_data_sources
tools.description: The public files behind the figures, when each was fetched, and where the method is described.
